findings.title: Stray submodule pointer committed as a regular file
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951...`. This looks like an accidental submodule/gitlink artifact unrelated to the feature. It will confuse checkouts and tooling, and it should not be merged.

findings.title: Cache key built from Python hash() of project IDs can collide and serve wrong eligibility
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, which is a 64-bit hash, not the project set itself. Two different project sets for the same organization that hash to the same value share one cache entry, so a query can be treated as all-allowlisted (or not) based on another query's result. The consequence is silently wrong error counts, since upsampled sums are returned for a non-allowlisted project set. Using the sorted tuple or a string of the IDs in the key avoids this.

findings.title: 60-second cache of allowlist eligibility makes upsampling decisions stale
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but the docstrings state the allowlist is read 'fresh each time' and that caching is 'safe'. Removing a project from the allowlist will still return upsampled counts for up to a minute. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` exists to address this, but nothing calls it, so the stale window is unavoidable. The documented guarantees in this module contradict the implementation.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code and cannot clear the real cache entries
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the PR. Even if it were, it only deletes the key for the exact project list passed in. Queries that use a subset or different ordering map to other keys, and the allowlist change path has no hook to call it. It should be removed or wired in.

findings.title: Cache-hit and cache-miss paths evaluate the dataset/query check differently and the allowlist is checked before the cheap dataset check
findings.body: On every request, including all non-error datasets (spans, transactions, metrics), the cache lookup and allowlist read happen before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` short-circuits. The dataset gate should run first so non-error queries skip the cache and option work entirely.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset and original request query, not the query actually executed
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the endpoint-level `dataset` and `request`, but `_get_event_stats` may run against `scoped_dataset` (e.g. discover for split dashboard widgets) with a rewritten query such as `(query) AND !event.type:transaction`. `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, not the query being run. So a widget split into error events can run a discover query that is not upsampled, while the same query in another path is upsampled, giving inconsistent counts. The decision should be based on the dataset and query actually passed in.

findings.title: Unrelated change to public error message text
findings.body: The error detail changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is outside the scope of error upsampling, changes an API response string that clients or tests may match on, and is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Comments claim caching gives consistent behavior, which is not true
findings.body: The comments say 'This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and 'allows for better query optimization and caching'. The eligibility is cached for 60 seconds and the transform is a pure column rewrite, so neither statement is accurate. The comments also describe a late transform that is actually the same logic duplicated in three branches. These comments will mislead maintainers.

findings.title: Redundant reassignment of final_columns across three branches
findings.body: `final_columns` is initialized to `query_columns` and then re-derived in up to three separate places with the same condition. Only one path runs per call, so this adds state and maintenance risk without benefit. A single computed value before the branches would be clearer and avoids the chance of one branch being updated and another missed.

findings.title: upsampled_count assumes sample_weight is never null, which the test factories do not guarantee
findings.body: The comment says sample_weight is guaranteed for allowlisted projects, but the factory change only sets sample_rate when the event contains an error_sampling context. Events without that context, which are common in tests and possibly in production, may have null or missing sample_weight. `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` over nulls can then return zero or error. Relying on an unverified schema invariant without a null guard is risky.

findings.title: Helper swallows all exceptions silently and changes store_event behavior globally
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps reads and conversions in bare `except Exception: pass`, hiding malformed fixtures. It is also called from the shared `store_event` factory used by the whole test suite, so every test that stores events with a contexts.error_sampling payload has its sample_rate silently altered. The change should be scoped to the tests that need it, and failures should not be swallowed.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the discover-split, cache, or non-allowlisted-with-error-query paths that the implementation changes
findings.body: The new endpoint tests only cover the top-level discover query with event.type:error and transactions. They do not exercise the dashboard widget split branch where scoped_dataset and the query differ, the cache hit path (including stale-after-allowlist-change behavior), or the topEvents path where upsampling is applied to timeseries columns. The unit tests in test_error_upsampling.py also do not test `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` or its caching at all. The highest-risk new logic is therefore untested.
